articles.title: Charles Leclerc wins F1 British Grand Prix behind safety car
articles.summary: Charles Leclerc collects his first victory of the 2026 F1 season after late safety car confusion in the final laps.
articles.body:
Charles Leclerc gave Ferrari their 250th Grand Prix victory on Sunday when he won a gripping British GP at Silverstone, which ended with a safety car as championship leader Kimi Antonelli missed out on a top 10 finish.

Antonelli’s Mercedes teammate and championship rival George Russell came through to take second place, while Lewis Hamilton in the other Ferrari crossed the line in third.

Nine-time Silverstone winner Hamilton was later put under investigation for a yellow flag infringement, having already served a five-second penalty for a false start.

Antonelli, who won the sprint on Saturday, still leads the title race with 179 points, 25 ahead of Russell, with Hamilton a further seven points back in third.

It was Leclerc’s ninth Grand Prix victory – and first since he won the United States GP in Austin in October 2024 – putting him fourth in the championship with 108 points.

“Finally, this one feels particularly good,” said Leclerc over the radio after taking the chequered flag.

“I wish for a bit more normal ending. Hard work paid off, hard times never last, only tough people last.”

Antonelli began on pole but was overtaken by both Ferraris at the start before battling back to make it a dogfight with Leclerc.

On lap 42 of 52, the 19-year-old Italian reported a problem and was forced into the pits.

When he came out he limped on before returning to the pits, where the mechanics removed a brake cooling inlet. It didn’t help him and, combined with a five-second penalty, he could only finish 16th.

Max Verstappen looked a dead cert for the podium, running a strong third when his Red Bull flew off the track and into the gravel on lap 48 of 52.

However, a McGregor toe injury forced a postponement and the match was never rescheduled.

McGregor, 37, returns to the welterweight division for the first time in ⁠six years. The Irishman is looking to re-establish himself as a title contender while attempting to defeat Holloway for the second time, following a unanimous decision victory over him in August 2013 at a UFC Fight Night event in Boston in McGregor’s second UFC fight.

Holloway (27-9 MMA) is making his official welterweight debut after a historic run at 145lb (65.5kg) and 155lb (70.5kg) over the last decade-plus.

McGregor said he is grateful for the opportunity to reinvigorate his career and has no immediate plans to change weight divisions after the Holloway rematch.

“The OG champ-champ, coming for the triple crown,” McGregor told reporters ‌at Thursday’s pre-fight news conference. “Sounds like a hell of a story to me.”

Following the loss of his “BMF” title to former lightweight champion Charles Oliveira at UFC 326 in March, Holloway, 34, hopes to avenge the loss to McGregor and immediately enter the 170-pound (77kg) title picture should he opt not to return to lightweight.

“We’re gonna find out Saturday night,” Holloway said in response to McGregor’s claim that he won’t “lay a glove” on him.

McGregor said he was not pleased with Holloway’s “disrespectful” comments about offering a potential December rematch, ensuring it will not be needed.

In response, Holloway fired back, igniting ⁠the rivalry even further.

What happened in the first McGregor vs Holloway fight?

McGregor defeated Holloway via unanimous decision (30-27, 30-27, 30-26) on August 17, 2013 at UFC Fight Night 26 in Boston.

The fight took place before they became global stars and was on the preliminary card that evening.

McGregor’s striking proved to be a problem for Holloway early in the fight, and he wobbled the Hawaiian with a big uppercut in the second round. But the second half of the fight mostly took place on the ground, with McGregor enjoying enough control to see out the win.

articles.title: WNBA coach Brondello suspended over inappropriate comment at Angel Reese
articles.summary: Brondello suspended for a game after calling Reese a ‘protected species’ in Toronto Tempo’s game against Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
Toronto Tempo coach Sandy Brondello was suspended for one game by the WNBA for an inappropriate comment she used during a game against the Atlanta Dream on Friday.

“The WNBA expects all coaches and team personnel to uphold the highest standards of professionalism and respect that are fundamental to our league,” the league said on Saturday in a statement announcing the suspension.

She’ll miss Monday’s game against the Las Vegas Aces.

During the 111-92 loss to the Dream, the broadcast picked up the Tempo’s coach addressing officials after Toronto player Nyara Sabally went down with an injury after contact with Angel Reese. Sabally was called for the foul and Brondello could be heard saying Reese was a “protected species”.

Brondello posted an apology on social media on Saturday.

“Angel, I’m sorry,” Brondello said. “Last night, in the emotion of the moment after Nyara’s injury, I used a phrase that I shouldn’t have used, and I take full responsibility for that. My frustration was with the officiating, but my words unfairly put the focus on you.”

Reese took to social media after the game, posting: “ARE WE SURPRISED?!” and tagging Brondello’s account, followed by a clown face emoji.

“I also understand that my words carried an impact beyond what I intended, particularly for Black women in our league, and I’m deeply sorry for that,” Brondello posted.

“I’ve spent my career competing with, coaching and learning from incredible Black women.”

The coach added: “I regret that my words caused hurt to a community I respect so deeply. I have a lot of respect for you as both a player and a person, and I sincerely apologize to you, your teammates, and the Dream organization for my comment.”

Brondello, who is in her first season with the expansion Tempo, is Australian. The “protected species” phrase is used in Australian sports to express frustration for a lack of calls against a player. However, in the US, the phrase suggests that someone isn’t human and could be seen as derogatory towards Black people.

Brondello has been a head coach in the league since 2014, winning titles with Phoenix and New York.

Russell had been the 19-year-old Italian’s closest rival before the start at Spa-Francorchamps, but the Briton spun off into the gravel on the opening lap after a collision with Hamilton while trying to make up places lost at lights out.

articles.title: The World Cup is over, long live the World Cup: A look back at one of the best tournaments ever
articles.summary: And just like that, the 2026 World Cup is over. After 308 goals were scored during 104 matches in 16 host cities across three continents, it was Spain that lifted the trophy.
articles.body: Note: This story first appeared in The Beautiful Game by CNN Sports, our daily newsletter on all things World Cup. While we’re saying goodbye for now, we will be back for the European domestic club season. See you then! And just like that, the 2026 World Cup is over. After 308 goals were scored during 104 matches in 16 host cities across three countries, it was Spain that lifted the trophy. And while the final wasn’t exactly one for the neutral, it was fitting that the best team in the tournament won in the end. But while La Roja supporters around the world celebrated the country’s second title (Spanish editor’s note: my headache and I can confirm this occurred in North London), everyone else was left reflecting on an emotional, record-breaking, superstar-studded edition of the tournament. For years, there were so many concerns around this World Cup. Would it be safe? Would the locals care? Would it be a waste of money? And while those critics were proved right at times, the 2026 edition can still be considered a resounding success. And that’s not down to the politicians or governing bodies; it’s down to the millions of fans who flocked to North America to party with one another. It’s down to the superstars who turned up and performed at the highest level and to the tournament minnows who punched well above their weight. So, in our last World Cup edition of this newsletter, it only feels right to remember some of the most magical moments. The Main Thing: And the award goes to… Before Spain got its hands on the main trophy, there were also several individual awards handed out at the end of yesterday’s final. France’s Kylian Mbappé was named the winner of the Golden Boot after scoring 10 goals – becoming the World Cup’s all-time top scorer in the process. Spanish defender Pau Cubarsí was named the best young player, Unai Simón was awarded the Golden Glove for best goalkeeper and midfielder Rodri won the Golden Ball for player of the tournament. But while those official awards have already been decided, we at The Beautiful Game wanted to recognize some of our own winners. Treat this as CNN’s World Cup Oscars. You may disagree with some decisions, but that’s OK because I’m quite tired. Best Game Sorry, Spain fans, but it certainly wasn’t the final. Fortunately, though, we were treated to some incredible soccer matches over the past month and change. The first game that springs to my mind is England’s heroic effort against Mexico in the Estadio Azteca. Down to 10 men, fighting altitude and fervent home support, the Three Lions somehow clung on against the co-host to reach the quarterfinals. We then had the likes of Cape Verde drawing against Uruguay, 2-2, and then the Blue Sharks again pushing defending champion Argentina to extra-time in the Round of 32. But, on balance, I think we’re given this to the Albiceleste’s 3-2 comeback against Egypt in the Round of 16. It had everything. Controversy galore, brilliant goals and a Lionel Messi-shaped miracle comeback. At least you won something, Argentina fans… Best Goal This is usually a hard category to decide, but I actually think it’s quite simple this year. The award goes to Cape Verde’s Sidny Lopes Cabral for his wondergoal against the Albiceleste in the knockout stages. There are a few reasons why this was so special. First, the strike itself was superb. He first beat his marker out wide before cutting in and bending his effort into the top corner of the net. Then consider the context. The goal was in extra-time against Messi’s Argentina. All of a sudden, Cape Verde fans started to believe in miracles. And then there was his celebration. Cabral was so excited that he ran into the crowd looking for someone he knew to celebrate with. It was an iconic moment that will be remembered for quite some time. Biggest Upset This one has caused some debate within the team. Not to keep banging on about Cape Verde, but not many expected the tiny island nation to play so well, so most of its results look like upsets on paper. Then you have Curaçao, the smallest nation to ever play in the competition, who managed to hold onto a draw against Ecuador in the group stages. But after much deliberation, I’m giving this to Paraguay for beating Germany in the Round of 32. Now I know the Germans are struggling a bit with their current crop of players, but they definitely should have beaten Paraguay on paper alone. The South Americans, though, somehow went ahead in the match and relied on a fighting spirit to restrict Germany to only one goal in reply. After defending that draw with their life, the Albirroja then beat the European powerhouse on penalties (something that very few have done before). Quote of the Day A quick break from the awards show to give you a sense of what the World Cup win meant to Spain. These are the words from goalscorer Ferrán Torres, who won the final for his country after scoring the only goal of the game. Torres, 26, said he felt the entire population of Spain behind him as he lashed his extra-time effort into the back of the net and it couldn’t have happened to a more deserving person. Torres – one of Barcelona’s key men up front – had been having an awful tournament, missing a plethora of chances throughout the campaign and being benched after starting against Cape Verde. The Barça attacker came through in the clutch, bringing joy to an entire nation that had almost abandoned him. WATCH: Fans react to Spain winning the World Cup If you still don’t understand how much soccer means to fans around the world, then just watch this. Spanish supporters filled the streets of Madrid to celebrate the country’s second World Cup title after the team beat Argentina. CNN en Español’s Pau Mosquera was in and amongst the bedlam in the capital. Awards continued Biggest Controversy Right, back to the awards and, sadly, a few contenders for this category. Even before a ball was kicked, there were plenty of headlines. First, Somali referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan was denied entry into the United States, meaning his dream tournament came to an end before it even began. Then we had the appalling treatment of the Iranian national team, which had to change training bases at the last minute and then fly between its base in Mexico and the US in order to play its games. But the moment that caused the biggest uproar was the red card decision around USA star Folarin Balogun. More notably, the fact that Donald Trump took it upon himself to try to overturn the decision. It was a stark insight into how those with power see the world. In no way should Trump be getting involved in such a thing, and there is even less reason FIFA should have listened. It contributed to a sad ending for the US team, which played so well at times and inspired a new generation to get into the sport of soccer. No real winners for this category, then. Biggest Star And finally, which of the players stood out the most. We have a few contenders for this one. Messi, of course, was superb and rolled back the years to produce some mesmerizing performances. We then have Mbappé who showed once again why he’s probably the most effective player at international tournaments – there is just something special about his game at World Cups and European Championships. Then we have to consider the likes of England’s Jude Bellingham who was just immense for the Three Lions and Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha who became an overnight star. But, after plenty of discussion, I’m going to surrender to the internet memes and give this award to Erling Haaland. The Norwegian striker did the business on the pitch, let’s get that straight first. He took his team to the quarterfinals, beating five-time champion Brazil on the way and scoring some big goals. But his larger-than-life personality also endeared him to people across the world, many of whom didn’t even watch the games. The Haaland memes and video clips were everywhere. Lookalike events popped up all around the world and people fell in love with the 25-year-old’s approach to, well, everything. “I’m quite happy with my life,” he said after bowing out of the competition. Lifetime Achievement Well, one last category – because that’s what these sorts of award shows do, right? It’s basically just an excuse to recognize Lionel Messi for everything he has done for soccer and answer the question that many people have: Is he now retiring from the international game? In truth, we don’t know yet. At 39, he’s clearly not able to compete physically against the best in the world during an entire match. But he does still show flashes of brilliance that make you think he can keep playing. The tears at the end of the final, though, suggest where his mind might be at. He has nothing left to prove and has won everything he possibly can. He’ll probably take some time to reflect but, yes, there is a chance that’s the last time we see Messi in an Argentina jersey. But we have said that before. Don’t fear, though. The Argentine is still contracted to play for Inter Miami until 2028, so he’ll surely honor that and be back on a soccer pitch again soon. The Final Whistle: The Beautiful Game bids farewell… for now And just a final note from me as we wrap this newsletter up for the World Cup. There has been so much to talk about, break down and reflect on during this tournament and I hope you got something out of this daily drop. We hope to be back in the not-so-distant future once the world’s biggest domestic leagues get back up and running, but more on that soon. For the time being, we’re off to sit on a beach for a couple weeks and reflect on what has been one of the best summers of sport. ¡Adios! The Trophy Lift: CNNers show their love for the World Cup And the last word goes to CNNers from all around the world who tuned in to watch all the action unfold. We hope you enjoyed the tournament as much as we did.

articles.title: Where will LeBron James go next? NBA star ‘not rushed’ to make a decision
articles.summary: Reports have linked James to the Golden State Warriors, the Philadelphia 76ers, the Miami Heat, or the Cleveland Cavaliers.
articles.body:
LeBron James’s longtime agent says the NBA ‌‌superstar will decide on his next team when he’s good and ready.

“We’re not going to ⁠⁠be rushed,” Rich Paul ⁠⁠said on Monday night’s episode of his Game Over podcast with sports broadcaster Max Kellerman. “We’re not going to be rushed. It’s his choice to make, and when he makes the choice, ⁠⁠he’ll make it.”

Paul also said that the teams that are courting the 22-time All-Star do not need to provide any more information at this time.

“There’s been several people to call and say, ‘Hey, Rich, ⁠⁠is there anything more we should be doing? We could be doing?'” he said. “And my answer is, ‘No. We don’t need you to go above and beyond about anything. We understand it. It’s clear. All the messages have been sent.'”

Tuesday marked three weeks since Paul told the Los Angeles Lakers that the 41-year-old forward was not ‌‌returning to the team for his record-setting 24th NBA season and was entering free agency.

Potential landing spots for the NBA’s all-time leading scorer include the Golden State Warriors and Philadelphia 76ers or a possible return to the Miami Heat or Cleveland Cavaliers, ESPN reported.

“I won’t hold you guys up too much longer,” James said during a public appearance in New York last week.

Paul said he addressed the situation with NBA commissioner Adam Silver, who said last Thursday that he wanted the ⁠⁠four-time league MVP and four-time NBA champion “to make his announcement already, so ⁠⁠we can finish the schedule”.

“I saw Adam in New York, and we discussed it,” Paul said. “And like I said, it’s still his choice. So if he doesn’t really know, you can’t rush it. You can’t rush it.”

On the podcast, Paul insisted ⁠⁠that James is not dragging out the process to build suspense, as was the case with his televised announcement in 2010 — hyped as “The Decision” — that he ⁠⁠was leaving the Cavaliers to join the Heat.

“I think it’s ⁠⁠important for people to understand: We’re not making this about attention and a spectacle,” Paul said. “It’s not about a ‘decision’ or anything like that. He has a choice to make. He has a business choice to make. We’re not going to sit here and ‌‌decide or allow someone else to decide when he makes that decision. … It’s a business choice that he’s making. And I think as an athlete, why is it that an athlete has to rush ‌‌his ‌‌choice?”

James averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds in 60 games with the Lakers in 2025–26. He owns career averages of 26.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 7.4 assists in a record 1,622 games with three teams.

articles.title: World Matchplay Darts: Luke Littler blows Josh Rock away and Dirk van Duijvenbode wins thriller against Gary Anderson to set up semi-final showdown
articles.summary: Luke Littler averaged 109.57 in a comprehensive display against Josh Rock; he will take on Dirk van Duijvenbode who won a thrilling match against Gary Anderson; you can watch the World Matchplay live on Sky Sports in Blackpool until July 26
articles.body:
Luke Littler stormed into the semi-finals of the World Matchplay, thumping Josh Rock to set up a meeting with Dirk van Duijvenbode, who came through a thriller against Gary Anderson.

Litter beat Rock 16-7 as he looks to become the first person to go back-to-back at this tournament since Michael van Gerwen a decade ago.

In what is turning into a tournament for the record books, Littler's stats impressed once again. He posted a 109.57 average with 17 180s and a 53 per cent success rate on the doubles.

"Another brilliant game for myself. I've gone 109, 113, 109 again [averages] so I've just got to keep it going," Littler told Sky Sports.

"Fair play to Josh. He gave me a really good game there. I think it was the third session where I won all five legs.

"I kind of got myself into that lead and I just had to stay there and got the job done."

Littler and Rock met at the semi-final stage of this tournament just one year ago when Littler won an 18-15 epic, hitting a nine-darter on way.

However after a close opening 10 legs to get Thursday's match going, it was all Littler as he romped into another semi-final.

Rock was in the zone early in the contest and matched every break of throw that was thrown at him, a 129 checkout from 'The Nuke' a highlight as the pair of young stars looked in a real battle at 5-5.

However, as is now customary from Littler, he took control in second session to reel off five legs in a row. Remarkably, Rock did not get a dart at double in that period.

He increased that dominance to seven legs in a row before Rock could stop the onslaught. Two holds of throw were all that the Northern Irishman managed as he sat 13-6 behind.

The final blow then came in the 23rd leg when the 19-year-old broke Rock's throw again as he cleaned up 44.

With that, the defending champion came to hold his throw and with his third match dart, took his favourite D10.

Van Duijvenbode holds on after Anderson rally

Van Duijvenbode held off a phenomenal fightback from Anderson in a 16-13 thriller to book a spot in the semi-finals in Blackpool for the first time in his career.

The Dutchman was 15-8 ahead, just one from victory, when Anderson roared back and averaged over 114 to take five legs in a row including a massive 154 checkout. It looked like he simply was going to pull off a miracle.

However, just when he needed it, Van Duijvenbode found his form to pin D10 for a massive win.

"To be fair the break couldn't come at a worse moment. You just know Gary loves the game. He never gives up," Van Duijvenbode told Sky Sports.

"He's probably the best in the world when he hits the trebles.

"I expected [the 154]. He didn't miss, but I always think my opponent will hit it."

The Dutchman added: "At some point I felt nerves in my stomach."

The opening session went the way of Van Duijvenbode, with the Dutchman finding two breaks of throw and finishing off the five legs with a 107 checkout to romp into a 4-1 lead.

The second session was similar to the first and when Van Duijvenbode found another break of throw and followed it with a clutch 112 checkout, it was looking ominous for Anderson with his opponent 8-3 ahead.

Anderson had work to do and he got going by taking out three legs on the spin, including a clutch bullseye finish for 84, to get back into the contest.

Van Duijvenbode stopped the rot with a hold of throw but had been reeled back into a contest at 9-6.

That was until Van Duijvenbode came back out on fire while the Flying Scotsman fell away in the next session with the Dutchman taking all five legs.

Anderson's throw was broken three times with a miracle looking the only option for the former world champion as he sat 14-6 behind.

And so nearly did a miracle occur. Anderson showed just he is one of the greats of the game, but Van Duijvenbode found the singular moment he needed to finally get over the line.

What is happening on Friday at the World Matchplay Darts?

The quarter-finals continue on Friday at the World Matchplay, live from 7.30pm on Sky Sports Main Event and Action.

Gian van Veen and James Wade will do battle in the quarter-finals for a second year in a row, with the world No 3 looking to avenge his loss to 'The Machine' in 2025.

Then, Gerwyn Price faces Ross Smith. Smith is through to the quarter-finals after Cameron Menzies withdrew from their second round match in the fourth leg due to illness.

articles.body:

He has and then some. The numbers are jaw-dropping:

  • 109 average in second round and quarter-finals
  • Nine-darter vs Nathan Aspinall

"He can play in spells. I say spells because he's been doing it all tournament. I was delighted for Josh because it was an improved performance and a 101 average but he lost by nine legs so it just shows how good Littler is," Webster said.

"He looks comfortable in every scenario. Good luck to Dirk on Saturday.

articles.body:
LeBron James is heading to the Philadelphia 76ers.

James made the announcement on social media Friday, saying it will be his “last decision” and that it comes after he strongly considered retirement.

articles.title: Fury dominates Wach in Thailand boxing bout ahead of Joshua showdown
articles.summary: Tyson Fury forced his Polish opponent, Mariusz Wach, to retire in the fight at a Muay Thai stadium in Pattaya, Thailand.
articles.body:
Former world heavyweight champion Tyson ⁠⁠Fury ⁠⁠forced Polish opponent Mariusz Wach to retire in a tune-up ⁠⁠bout for his showdown with ⁠⁠fellow Briton Anthony Joshua later this year.

The fight in Thailand on Friday was not televised, but will feature in the Netflix reality ‌‌show, At Home with the Furys. About 1,500 fans attended the event at the Max Muay Thai Stadium in Pattaya.

Wach had lost seven of his last ⁠⁠10 fights, and the ⁠⁠46-year-old could not continue at the start of the eighth round.

Fury, who ⁠⁠turns 38 in August, has won 36 ⁠⁠professional bouts, suffering his ⁠⁠only losses in two fights with Ukraine’s Oleksandr Usyk in 2024.

He announced his return to boxing in January, having retired from the sport in December 2024 after losing to Oleksandr Usyk in a bout for three of the four major world titles.

Fury is a two-time world champion. He ended the reign of Wladimir Klitschko with a points win in 2015 that saw him crowned Super WBA, IBF and WBO champion.

He didn’t fight again until 2018 – but a thrilling trilogy with American Deontay Wilder resulted in a draw and two victories for him to claim the WBC title.

The British star confirmed his comeback in a post on social media, which sets up the prospect of a long-awaited showdown with Anthony Joshua.

Joshua, also a ‌‌former world heavyweight champion, is set to face Kristian Prenga in ‌‌Saudi ‌‌Arabia on Saturday.

articles.title: Luke Littler: World Matchplay defending champion believes he can dominate like Phil Taylor ahead of semi-final
articles.summary: Luke Littler stormed into the semi-finals of the World Matchplay with a thumping win over Josh Rock and has set his sights on dominating the sport in the same fashion as Phil Taylor; you can watch the World Matchplay live on Sky Sports in Blackpool until July 26
articles.body:
Luke Littler says he will dominate darts in the same way Phil Taylor did if he continues his sparkling form.

A scintillating Littler progressed to the semi-finals of the World Matchplay on Thursday with a dominant 16-7 win over Josh Rock, averaging 109.57 with a 53 per cent success rate on the doubles.

On Saturday 'The Nuke', who scored 17 180s against Rock in Blackpool, will face Dirk van Duijvenbode in the semi-final - live on Sky Sports.

The world No 1 is aiming to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen in 2016 to go back-to-back in Blackpool, with few betting against him.

Immediately after Thursday's win, he said: "I feel really good up on the stage, preparations beforehand are going really well, just relaxing, playing, relaxing again. I'm just glad I can perform on the biggest stages."

articles.title: World Matchplay darts: Gerwyn Price issues title warning to 'ruthless' Luke Littler after reaching Blackpool semi-finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler remains pre-tournament favourite to defend his title at the World Matchplay; Gerwyn Price faces Gian van Veen in Saturday's semi-finals as he looks to reach his first Blackpool final since 2022; watch throughout the weekend live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Gerwyn Price insists he can thwart Luke Littler's bid for back-to-back World Matchplay titles and believes some players ‘make it too easy’ for the defending champion.

Price booked his first World Matchplay semi-final since 2022 with a 16-12 win over Ross Smith at the Winter Gardens, where the 'Ice Man' fired a 102.78 average and closed out victory with a four-leg burst.

The Welshman faces world No 3 Gian van Veen in the last four, with the winner of that semi-final progressing to face either Littler or Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode in Sunday's best-of-35 leg final.

  • Latest World Matchplay Darts results, schedule 📅
  • Gerwyn Price books semi-final spot - as it happened
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

Littler defeated Price in every Premier League fixture between them this season and a final-set decider in the World Masters semi-finals, while 'The Nuke' remains unbeaten in PDC major matches over 20 legs since his 2024 World Championship final loss.

The world No 1 remains overwhelming favourite to become the first player since Michael van Gerwen to defend his World Matchplay crown, having posted a 109.57 average in his win over Josh Rock, although Price insists he can be stopped.

"I think there's a lot of players that can get to that [Littler's] level," Price told reporters after his quarter-final win.

"Is there anyone who can do it as long as him? I think I can and I think there's a couple of players, but he's ruthless at the minute - these 109, 110 averages just look so easy for him.

"I think some players play into his hand and just let him play with his rhythm. It's horses for courses, and sometimes you have to play your game, you have to play the game and you have to play the moments.

"Sometimes, people make it a little bit too easy for him."

More to come in Van Veen showdown?

Price built a commanding 12-8 lead over Smith in a quarter-final where he threatened to pull further ahead, then found himself level at 12-12 until finishing strongly to reach the last four.

"I was delighted with the way I played the majority of the game, but there's a couple of legs that I let slip and could have come back to haunt me in the end," Price added.

"I'm thinking I should be 13-7 or 14-6 or whatever it is, because I did waste opportunities and probably shouldn't think like that. I'm just happy to get a win, but frustrated a little bit."

Van Veen admitted he needs to improve after his quarter-final victory over 16-13 James Wade, where he posted a 93 average and also blew a four-leg advantage before closing out victory.

"It felt very poor!" Van Veen admitted to Sky Sports. "My scoring was so terrible. I was so lucky James wasn't scoring as well and my finishing got me through. A win is a win.

"The 118 finish - I really needed it. It was a tight battle but I'm glad I got the job done. Hopefully tomorrow I will be a lot better."

What's next?

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens on Saturday, with the two semi-finals being played over the best-of-33 to decide who progresses through to Sunday's best-of-35 final.

Defending champion Littler continues his bid for back-to-back titles when he faces Van Duijvenbode, through to the last four at this event for the first time, with Price playing Van Veen in the opening semi-final.

articles.title: Scrutiny of WNBA intensifies as disarray looms over All-Star festivities
articles.summary: Discussions about race, gender and sexuality overshadow Saturday’s WNBA All-Star Game, as league lurches into disarray.
articles.body:
More people are watching. More are investing. Salaries for many players are higher than ever. But mounting turmoil and discord have been a part of this transformative period that has featured a landmark collective bargaining agreement, league expansion and skyrocketing player recognition.

It seems to have reached a new flashpoint, as discussions about race, gender and sexuality created headlines ahead of Saturday’s WNBA All-Star Game. Race-driven conversations resurfaced after an incident between Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark and Phoenix Mercury forward Alyssa Thomas, while players continue to voice frustrations with WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert and leadership over what they say is a lack of protection from social media harassment and divisive remarks.

“It is a moment to be celebrated without a doubt,” said Ketra Armstrong, sport management professor and director of the Center for Race and Ethnicity in Sport at the University of Michigan. “We want to celebrate what’s great. But sometimes, the progress can overshadow, still, where the perils are.”

Issues of race, gender and representation have been an undercurrent throughout the league’s history. Debates over those issues have grown as women’s sports have exploded. And they remain a challenge that shapes the WNBA’s – and most other pro sports leagues, for that matter – public and online discourse.

“This is what a sports league” is, said David Berri, sports economist and economics professor at Southern Utah University. He cited the NFL’s Rooney Rule as an example. “If a sports league is going to get attention, you’re going to get attention for these things as well.”

Growth has magnified broader cultural debates

Contentious conversations also spread to issues of transgender athletes and harassment.

WNBA veteran Brianna Turner said on social media this week that her former team, the Fever, fired a male employee last season for sexual harassment. Turner, who was with Indiana last season but now plays for Las Vegas, also said Indiana players were encouraged not to discuss the firing.

Turner’s comments came as she defended transgender athletes days after Indiana forward Sophie Cunningham spoke on transgender athletes competing in women’s sports.

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I’m like, ‘I never once said that’,” Cunningham was quoted as saying in a story published by ESPN. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

The WNBA’s conversations about race were thrust back into the spotlight after Toronto Tempo coach Sandy Brondello was suspended one game for referring to Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese as a “protected species”.

The comment, picked up by the broadcast after Reese drew a foul on Toronto player Nyara Sabally, quickly drew criticism.

Brondello, a former player who has won two WNBA titles, is Australian. The “protected species” phrase is used in Australian sports to express frustration over a lack of calls against a player. However, in the US, the phrase suggests that someone isn’t human and could be seen as derogatory towards Black people. Brondello later apologised. Reese accepted it, saying she appreciated the league’s swift action.

“It’s a much bigger platform now. Everything that happens is news,” Berri said. “There were hard fouls 10 years ago. Nobody paid any attention to that. It ends up being because of the coverage now, everything gets magnified … which is good. I mean, this is what we wanted.”

‘A lot to celebrate’ but race still matters

Clark has repeatedly attempted to downplay the noise surrounding her, but she has become a springboard for projections far beyond the game itself.

“It’s basketball,” she said in a recent ESPN interview. “When I walk out of the locker room, I shouldn’t be fearful of what the conversation is going to be. It’s emotionally exhausting. It’s draining. It makes your shoulders tense because people don’t want to talk about the basketball. They just want to stir it up and make something else.”

The WNBA retroactively assessed Thomas a flagrant foul and suspended her one game after the veteran made contact with her fist to Clark’s throat in a June 24 matchup.

The play, which Thomas has said was an accident, gained widespread attention and ignited debates over officiating, with coaches, pundits and lawmakers weighing in on whether the league needs to take action about physical play involving Clark.

Thomas, who is Black and in her 12th WNBA season, said after the incident she had received death threats, part of increased online vitriol players have faced in recent years. Chelsea Gray of the Las Vegas Aces recently posted a message from a man that included a racial slur. And Engelbert this week met with a pair of player committees to discuss what more can be done to protect players from online harassment.

Since she entered the league, Clark and her WNBA peers have become proxies for longstanding American issues – from race, gender and sexual orientation to who receives attention and who doesn’t.

“There’s a lot to celebrate,” Armstrong said, “but race still matters. Race will always matter. It just depends on how we make it matter.”

articles.title: F1 needs better balance between business and sport, says Norris
articles.summary: Lando Norris speaks up ahead of Hungarian Grand Prix with drivers feeling new regulations have cramped their speed.
articles.body:
Formula One has been driven too much by business decisions and needs to remember it is a sport, according to McLaren’s world champion Lando Norris.

With drivers chafing ⁠at new regulations that have cramped their speed, particularly at last weekend’s Belgian Grand Prix, the Briton told reporters ahead of Sunday’s Hungarian round that Formula One could do better.

list 2 of 4 Gymnast Langton, 19, concussed after headfirst crash at Commonwealth Games

list 3 of 4 Chad le Clos makes Commonwealth Games history with a record 19th medal

list 4 of 4 Scrutiny of WNBA intensifies as disarray looms over All-Star festivities

“It’s a business,” said the Briton. “Everyone wants to make money, so in order for Audi ⁠and other teams to come in we had to change these things. It’s a shame. It should never have been like that. But that’s how businesses work.”

Audi have entered the sport this season after taking over Swiss-based Sauber, with the German carmaker encouraged by new rules that have increased the electrical element of the power unit to near-parity with the internal combustion engine. The rules have been ‌tweaked for 2027 to reduce the electrical contribution.

“Formula One will always be great,” said Norris, whose car has a Mercedes engine. “It can just be better.

“Us as drivers just know it better than everyone else. The thing that’s a shame is that Formula One is too heavily led by the fact it’s a business nowadays and not how can you make the sport the best possible. It’s ‘how can you just make the most money as a business?’

“And that’s just not what it should simply be. That’s not how a sport should be run. The fact we have hybrids, 50-50 and all that, that’s just because ⁠more teams wanted to come in it and because you make more money.”

Norris said the ⁠Liberty Media-owned sport was also divided between fans who followed Formula One before the arrival of the popular Netflix docu-series “Drive to Survive” and those who have been drawn to it since.

“I think the fans you have nowadays, because they’re a lot more personality-based … and not simply of Formula One as a whole ⁠sport, I think there’s less interest in basically how the actual race goes, and more just ‘has the driver done well or not?'” he added.

“I think that’s just how the fans have changed over ⁠time, and that’s completely fine. But the biggest voice should always be ours ⁠as drivers … We have the best idea of how racing should be, how it can be, what’s possible, what’s not.

“We would just want the best for everything, the best for the fans, the best viewing, the best racing for us, the most fun to drive. And at the minute, we don’t … we have very, very ‌little say, and a lot more of it’s done because if you can have Audi and other teams in it, it’s a bigger win than the drivers being happy.”

A Formula One spokesman responded to Norris’s comments by saying drivers were listened to more ‌than ‌ever.

“The sport on track is, and always will be, the priority,” he said. “Everyone has benefitted from the commercial success of Formula One, the drivers included. Decisions are made for the best strategic outcome for everyone: the fans, teams and partners.”

Norris was ⁠fastest in final ⁠practice for the Hungarian Grand Prix on Saturday.

Last year’s race winner lapped the Hungaroring circuit with ⁠a best time of 1:17.939, 0.117 seconds quicker than Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton.

Formula One championship leader Kimi ⁠Antonelli was third fastest, 0.129 seconds off the pace and ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc, McLaren’s Oscar Piastri and Mercedes teammate George Russell.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen was seventh on the timesheets, ‌with teammate Isack Hadjar eighth but 1.004 off the pace.

articles.title: Commonwealth Games:  England cruise past Northern Ireland to open netball campaign as Scotland fall to New Zealand
articles.summary: England limber up for Sunday’s big Commonwealth Games netball clash against Australia by sweeping aside Northern Ireland in their opening group game; Eleanor Cardwell scored 35 goals and vice-captain Liv Tchine added 25
articles.body:
England thrashed Northern Ireland 83-34 on the opening day of the Netball pool stage at the Commonwealth Games but Scotland were beaten by New Zealand.

England ran out comfortable winners at The Hydro, with all 12 players taking to the court in a confidence-building performance.

"Getting that first win and performance under our belts was important," said Stembridge. "We'll make sure we close the loop in our debrief and then turn our full focus to Australia tomorrow."

"Australia are world No 1 for a reason, and we have a huge amount of respect for them," she continued.

"We feel well prepared and will be ready to respond to whatever tactics they bring. It's exciting to think about the matchups and the challenges we can pose as well.

Vice-captain Tchine added: "It was great to see everyone putting into practice what we've been working on in training. Everyone came out and gave everything.

"I think we needed that. We played together well and got those first-game nerves out of the way. Everyone knows what it's like in that opening match, so now we're ready to focus on Australia tomorrow."

articles.title: Joshua comes back twice to knock out Prenga and set up Fury showdown
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua survives two knockdowns by Albania’s Kristian Prenga before winning the fight in the second round.
articles.body:
Former two-time world champion Anthony Joshua recovered from two knockdowns to knock out Kristian Prenga in the second round of a dramatic non-title heavyweight fight in Saudi Arabia.

The fight in Jeddah on Saturday was seen as the British boxer’s final step before setting up a long-awaited showdown against his compatriot Tyson Fury.

It also marked his return to the ring for the first time since a horrific car crash in Nigeria in December, during which Joshua lost two of his best friends and sustained injuries.

Back inside the ring, Joshua was floored by an uppercut inside 30 seconds. He beat the count but looked seriously shaken.

Then Prenga knocked Joshua down again, but the former heavyweight champion rose before the end of the count and survived until the bell in the first round.

A quick end to the fight was expected, but nobody thought it would be Prenga’s.

In the second round, Joshua unleashed a flurry of punches and finished Prenga with a right hook, sending the Albanian through the bottom of the ropes.

The turnaround shocked even heavyweight king Oleksandr Usyk, whose face was caught by TV cameras as he watched from ringside.

The comeback kept alive the possibility of an all-British fight between Joshua and Fury.

Joshua’s manager Eddie Hearn claims his fighter and Fury have signed a contract to meet for the first time later this year, but on the condition that they come through warm-up bouts this weekend.

“I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat,” Joshua told the crowd about fighting Fury following his win over Prenga.

Fury played his part by coming out of retirement this year and, on Friday, forcing 46-year-old Polish journeyman Mariusz Wach to retire in round seven in Pattaya, Thailand.

Joshua almost blew his part of the claimed contract before showcasing his champion’s fightback spirit.

Prenga brought a 20-1 fight record with 20 KOs into the match-up with Joshua and looked every bit the knockout artist.

Joshua, fighting for the first time since surviving the car crash that killed his friends Sina Ghami and Latif ‘Latz’ Ayodele, acknowledged them straight after improving his fight record to 30-4 (27 KOs).

“It’s more than punch power,” Joshua said of his knockout punch. “That was spirit. That was Latz and Sina. That was the family. You know what I mean? That hurts even talking about it.

“He [Prenga] gave me a good test, but this is what champions do: we rise. We get knocked down and stand up. That is life; that is life’s motto.”

articles.title: Malaysia to host rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix F1 race in October
articles.summary: The race in Bahrain was rescheduled in April amid the US-Israel war on Iran and will now be held in Malaysia.
articles.body:
Malaysia’s Sepang circuit will host a rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix in October, Formula One has announced.

The Liberty Media-owned sport said in a statement on Sunday that the October 4 race at the circuit near Kuala Lumpur’s international airport would officially be designated the “Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia”.

“This is fantastic news for our fans,” Formula One Chief Executive Stefano Domenicali said while making the announcement at the Hungarian Grand Prix. He revealed that an agreement had been signed between the governments of Malaysia and Bahrain as well as the governing FIA and Formula One.

“They will continue to enjoy a full and exciting Formula One calendar, while also seeing the sport return to a great venue.

“Sepang holds a special place in Formula One history. It will provide a spectacular setting for racing and an unforgettable experience for fans at the circuit and watching around the world.”

The cancellations of April’s race at Sakhir, and the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Jeddah, were due to the United States and Israel’s war on Iran and its spillover in the Middle East.

The addition of Sepang takes the championship back to 23 races, although there is continuing speculation about whether the last two rounds of the season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will happen.

Italy’s Imola, a home circuit for Ferrari, is being considered as a replacement finale should those Middle Eastern races also not happen, according to informed sources at the Hungaroring.

The rescheduled Bahrain race, at a circuit that last hosted Formula One in 2017 and now serves as a MotoGP fixture, will slot in between the Azerbaijan Grand Prix on September 26 and Singapore on October 11.

There are several precedents for one country holding a race with the name of another: Germany’s Nurburgring hosted a Luxembourg Grand Prix, the San Marino Grand Prix was held for many years at Imola, and the Swiss Grand Prix was held in France.

Bahrain’s sovereign wealth fund Mumtalakat owns Formula One champions McLaren, and the Grand Prix is the kingdom’s biggest annual sporting event, serving to promote Bahrain internationally.

The country, home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet , has come under attack from Iranian missiles and drones.

The event remains subject to final agreements and approval of the FIA’s World Motor Sport Council.

articles.title: Lando Norris wins Hungarian Grand Prix for first F1 triumph in 2026
articles.summary: Defending champion Norris wins his first race of the year as Verstappen finishes second, and leader Antonelli third.
articles.body:
Lando Norris has ended an eight-month wait for a Formula One victory with strong pace and a dose of good fortune to win the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday.

McLaren’s defending champion finished ahead of Max Verstappen in Red Bull and teenage sensation Kimi Antonelli at the Hungaroring circuit in Budapest on Sunday.

Norris was on pole but lost the lead to his McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri when he ran wide at the second corner, before reclaiming the lead after Piastri was delayed by a collision with Carlos Sainz Jr during a lap.

This allowed Norris to come out of the pits ahead of his teammate and cruise to a win.

“The car was unbelievable today. Well done guys, incredible. We were flying,” Norris said. “Nice to finally be able to do it all for you. Feels like it’s been a while.”

Piastri then stopped with a broken gearbox, paving the way for Verstappen to take second, with Antonelli third.

Antonelli increased his standings lead, with title rival Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth after a penalty for speeding in the pits and George Russell seventh after a near-stall at the start.

Norris hadn’t won a full Grand Prix race since Sao Paulo in November, though he did win a sprint in Miami in May.

Hungary was the last race before the mid-season break. The next race is the Dutch Grand Prix on August 23.

articles.title: Commonwealth Games netball: England's Vitality Roses beaten by Australia in Glasgow for first defeat of tournament
articles.summary: England go down 66-47 to Australia on Sunday with captain Fran Williams saying her side were 'far off our best'; Vitality Roses return to action against Malawi on Monday as Group A campaign continues; England won Commonwealth Games gold in 2018 but did not medal at Birmingham 2022
articles.body:
England suffered their first defeat of the Commonwealth Games after going down 66-47 to reigning champions Australia in Glasgow.

The Vitality Roses trailed 18-11 after the first quarter and 35-24 at half-time before a series of handling errors helped Australia stretch their lead to 56-35 with 15 minutes left.

England won the final quarter 12-10 but the damage was already done as they were unable to back up their opening 83-34 victory over Northern Ireland on Saturday.

The top two sides in Groups A and B after all the sides have played the others in their pool once each will advance to the semi-finals.

Williams says England can take lessons from defeat

The Vitality Roses took Commonwealth Games gold on the Gold Coast in 2018, beating host nation Australia in the final, but did not medal in Birmingham four years ago.

Speaking after Sunday's defeat to Australia's Diamonds, England captain Fran Williams said lessons would be learned: "That's definitely not the result that we came for but it's also not the performance.

"We were far off our best and never really got momentum. It's really tough when a game blows out like that in the second half.

"You've got to make sure that you're still going after those small wins and little fights. That's why I'm so proud of the last 15 minutes in terms of getting a quarter win at the end when it was tough.

"It's great we've had that exposure against a team that's probably setting the standard in the competition. We've got the learning from the experience so we can move on.

"There's no point dwelling on it. It's about taking what we need from it and bringing it into [the Malawi match]. That will help us drop any disappointment. You've got to look forward."

articles.title: Women's World Matchplay: Beau Greaves defeats Fallon Sherrock in 6-5 last-leg decider to claim record third Blackpool crown
articles.summary: Beau Greaves came out on top against Fallon Sherrock with a 6-5 victory; it is a record-extending third Blackpool win; you can watch the World Matchplay final live on Sky Sports Action and Sky Sports Main Event from 7.30pm in Blackpool
articles.body:
Beau Greaves won the Women's World Matchplay for a record third time with a 6-5 last-leg victory over Fallon Sherrock at the Winter Gardens in Blackpool.

After Sherrock forced the contest the distance, Greaves held her nerve with a crucial 180 before a brilliant 145 left 56 for the title. She coolly pinned double 10 to seal victory once again.

The win adds to Greaves' 2023 and 2024 triumphs in this tournament. It was Sherrock that Greaves met in the 2024 Women's Matchplay final in which Greaves took the spoils in a 6-3 win.

It adds to an already impressive year for 'Beau and Arrow' in which she became the first woman to win a Pro Tour event at Players Championship 11. She also hit a nine-darter on the Tour and became the first woman to qualify for the European Tour.

The win for Greaves consigns Sherrock to runner-up at the Women's Matchplay for a third year in a row, losing to Greaves in 2024 and 2026 plus Lisa Ashton in 2025.

"I'm not one to celebrate but it was relief in the end. Fallon is a great lass and an even better darts player. I knew I had to play well but to hit that last dart was an outpouring of relief," Greaves told Sky Sports.

"Just so happy to win. I knew playing the women is a bit different because I play the men now. Chuffed just to get the win.

"I was nervous, but that kind of pressure is a privilege.

"I just love my life. love playing darts. I can't get enough of it. I'm addicted to it in a way and just love my life and even supporting the women's game is a massive thing.

"I love darts and it's good enough for me. My goal is to just play better."

It was billed as a close and enthralling contest between the two most successful players in women's darts, and it certainly lived up to expectations on the Winter Gardens stage.

Sherrock made the brighter start to the final, breaking throw in the third leg. But, in typical Greaves fashion, she hit back immediately to restore parity at 2-2 before producing a sensational 120 checkout in a 12-dart leg to move ahead.

From there, the contest developed into a gripping nip-and-tuck affair. A tense eighth leg eventually went Greaves' way as she pinned double two to secure a crucial break of throw and move within one leg of the title.

Sherrock, however, refused to go down without a fight. Some superb scoring left her on 36 after just nine darts, and she wrapped up an 11-dart break of throw. She then followed it with a classy 70 checkout on double 16 to force a deciding leg

That was when Greaves found her brilliant best once again with a maximum then silky 145 leaving her 56 for the title. On 56, she took double 10 to ensure the trophy was coming home with her.

Greaves' route to final: Brilliance and a battle!

Greaves had to battle hard to make it into the final in a 5-4 nerve-wracking victory over Gemma Hayter.

Greaves got off to slow start and Hayter made sure to capitalise, levelling the game at 2-2 with a break of throw on tops and then finding another crucial break with an 83 checkout on double 16 to take the game to a last-leg decider.

However, just when she needed it, Greaves came through with a massive 104 checkout to book her spot in a third Women's Matchplay final.

Greaves made it through to the semi-finals with a 5-1 victory over Kirsi Viinikainen, starting in imperious fashion with a 148 then 144 checkout to get the contest going.

Sherrock route to the final: One leg dropped!

Ashton's title defence came to an end when she ran into a clinical Sherrock who pulled off a 5-1 win to make her third straight Matchplay final in a row.

Indeed, it was a replay of the 2025 Matchplay final, but this time Greaves was firmly in control. Having dropped just a single leg en route to the final, she sealed her place in the showpiece match by pinning double 16.

Sherrock was also at her brilliant best in a 5-0 whitewash victory over Deta Hedman in the quarters, two 13-darters in a row the key as she gave the 'Caribbean Queen' no opportunities to counter attack and zero darts at the double.

Elsewhere, Hayter battled from 4-2 down to win a last-leg shootout against Vicky Pruim, overcoming some key errors to eventually pin a clutch 77 on tops for the match.

Meanwhile, the 'Lancashire Rose' Ashton began with a 5-2 win over Welsh No 1 Rhian O'Sullivan, a big 120 checkout for a break of throw the highlight before she eventually clinched the game with her ninth match dart.

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens on Sunday night, as defending champion Luke Littler takes on Gerwyn Price for the prestigious Phil Taylor Trophy.

articles.title: Beau Greaves: Have we seen the last of Doncaster star on the PDC Women’s Series? 'I'm focused on my Tour Card'
articles.summary: Beau Greaves opens up on playing the men and insists she must improve her stage game after winning the Women's World Matchplay in Blackpool; you can watch the BoyleSports World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports from September 28 to October 4 at the Mattioli Arena in Leicester
articles.body:
Have we seen the last of Beau Greaves on the PDC Women’s Series? 'Beau 'n Arrow' admits she felt "deflated" and felt "everybody wanted me to lose" after the 2025 edition.

Greaves claimed her third Women's World Matchplay title in four years as she edged out Fallon Sherrock 6-5 in a thrilling final in Blackpool.

The Doncaster arrowsmith kicked off her title bid with an assured 5-1 triumph over Finnish star Kirsi Viinikainen before surviving a scare against Gemma Hayter.

  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

Greaves set up a winner-takes-all clash with Sherrock in the final with 'The Queen of the Palace' taking back-to-back legs to level at 5-5 and force a decider.

They shared maximums but Greaves came out on top with a checkout of 56 to secure the crown.

Greaves has won a record 57 PDC Women's Series titles and discussing her future, the 22-year-old spoke about the difficulty of spinning between the men's and women's game.

"It's tough really," she said. "I think I've tried to just focus on the men's side, on my Tour Card. I think after the last Women's Series, I felt a bit deflated after it.

"I didn't really enjoy it too much. I just felt a bit like everybody wanted me to lose, so coming out of there I was like 'maybe I should just focus on playing better darts and more competitive darts and my ranking', just give me something to work towards.

"I think in the ladies game gets a bit stale for everybody because you're working towards this target and once you're there, there's nothing else to go towards.

"After the last one I was just thinking, 'I think now I'll concentrate on the Pro Tour and the Euro Tour that I've qualified for', just try and do that.

"I still love that side of the game, but now I think my main goal is the men's side and enjoy that part of it and the challenges that come with it."

Greaves' latest glory is only just the start with the World Youth finalist admitting she has got to focus on improving her stage game.

"I play darts for enjoyment but now it's my job, but I love the game. I cannot get enough of it, and to be able to support the ladies' game is a massive thing," said Greaves, who became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title with a historic 8-7 victory over Michael Smith in the Players Championship 11 final.

"I want to play even better. I win tournaments on the floor, but I think my stage game has got to improve and I know that."

'I'm really enjoying the challenge'

Greaves' victory on the Winter Gardens stage also secured her place in the 2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts and the 2027 Paddy Power World Darts Championship, after having featured in both tournaments last year.

"Obviously winning a Pro Tour really put me in the rankings. I've done well, quarter-finals, semi-finals, but it's tough," said Greaves.

"I think I'm really enjoying the challenge just to get there, to qualify for them and yeah, it'll be an achievement for me just to play there and just to say I have done it.

"I want to win, I want to do well, I need to work harder, I want to play better. I know I've got a long way to go before I'm really, really competitive with the men.

"I know I can do it, I just have to work harder for it and just put my mind to it, just believe in myself more than anything. I think sometimes I just doubt myself too much and it gets in the way of stuff.

"I enjoy the Pro Tour, the Euro Tour coming up, I look forward to them and it's tough, but it's good."

'I can beat anybody'

Greaves also sent out a warning to her rivals, saying she "never surprises herself" and she can "beat anybody" on her day.

"I think with me, it's just when and where it's going to turn up and that's something that is not a very good point in my game is that I am still very inconsistent, but I can be very consistent. It's just one of those things," said Greaves, who made more history on the PDC Pro Tour after qualifying for both the Hungarian Darts Trophy and Czech Darts Open.

"I know I can do it, I think sometimes I just get very happy in my own life and sometimes I forget that I need to do better, keep winning, keep doing that to prove to get up the rankings. I get very settled and that's my problem really."

"I will definitely take the positives," insisted Sherrock, who fell short in a last-leg decider in the showpiece for the second consecutive year.

"If somebody had said to me I'd get to the final, I'd have bitten their hand off.

"Beau deserved to win. She was the better player, so full credit to her.

articles.body:
Luke Littler has hailed his historic run at the World Matchplay as "one of the best weeks of his life" after a record-breaking 18-9 over Gerwyn Price in Blackpool.

It capped off a week in which Littler has broken record after record. The 19-year-old started his week with a 109 average against Niko Springer and then took things to new heights with a 113 average and nine-darter against Nathan Aspinall.

A 109 average against Josh Rock followed, before he demolished Dirk van Duijvenbode in the semi-finals.

Littler then became the first player in a decade to retain the title at the Winter Gardens, defeating Price while rewriting the record books in the process.

Littler fired an 111.53 average which smashed the tournament scoring record, previously set by Phil Taylor in 2010, leaving Littler continuing his run of winning every PDC TV major in 2026.

He also posted six ton-plus finishes and broke his own tournament record for most 180s, hitting 66 across the week.

Not only that, he broke the £3m earning barrier during his run to the final, with the latest win enhancing his hopes of sweeping every ranked major in a calendar year.

They are numbers to simply behold and Littler himself counts them as some of the best he has ever posted in his life.

"It has been a crazy week - it has been one of the best weeks of my life," Littler told Sky Sports.

"The darts I have played - it has not been easy. It has been tough. The stats may look like it is easy but when you are on this stage, it is hot, it is not easy.

"I have played some of the best darts of my life.

"Two years ago, I had that first round defeat to Michael which was not the best result, The last two years, I have come here with the family and we have done it again.

"It is definitely, I feel like it is the best version of myself. I have just been playing so well.

Littler: I am heading to the Pro Tours!

Littler said on the opening night of the World Matchplay that, if he defended his title, he would then have to head to the Pro Tour in order to attempt the clean sweep which would include having to defend his Players Championship Finals win in Minehead.

With that in mind, the world No 1's next stop is Leicester, rather than the planned trip to Spain.

"I don't think my dad is too happy because we were meant to be going to Spain but now we will be going to Leicester for some Pro Tours," he added.

"Coming into the tournament I had won every major so far so this is what I wanted to do.

Littler fired an 111.53 average and nailed 12 maximums in a dominant display against the 2022 runner-up, posting six ton-plus finishes in a high-scoring final to become just the fourth player in history to win back-to-back World Matchplay titles.

The winning margin looked set to be larger when Littler raced into an 11-3 lead, with Price - who averaged 104.97 in his performance of the tournament - delivering a battling display but falling to his second runner-up finish in four years.

Price said ahead of the final that he felt like he could beat Littler with his A-game, although the 'Ice Man' couldn't come close to his opponent during a historic final.

The first three legs went with throw before Littler followed a sensational 167 checkout - his first bullseye finish of this year's tournament - by taking out 110 to hold throw in the next, opening a 4-1 lead despite Price averaging over 109 in the mini session.

Price stayed within six legs of Littler before the 19-year-old produced another devastating late surge, firing in a stunning 148 checkout before breaking throw in the following leg. Littler then sealed a historic victory in style, pinning an 81 finish on the bullseye.

Victory is Littler's 10th consecutive win over Price and 28th consecutive win at PDC major matches over 20 legs, a run stretching back to the 2024 World Championship final, with the world No 1's record-breaking display sending an ominous warning to his rivals heading into the rest of the season.

articles.title: Luke Littler reaches new heights with World Matchplay run to remember: 'What can other players cling onto now?'
articles.summary: Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster believes Luke Littler produced the greatest World Matchplay campaign ever seen and has backed him to complete a clean sweep of the remaining majors in 2026
articles.body:
Sky Sports Darts' Mark Webster believes that Luke Littler's winning run at the World Matchplay is the "best major campaign we have ever seen" and with it, he has sent a message to the rest of his competitors.

Littler capped off a record-breaking week with a dominant 18-9 win over Gerwyn Price in the final, setting a new record average in a final of 111.53.

He also broke his own record for the number of 180s hit across the tournament, improving his 64 in 2025 to 66 in 2026.

  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

The victory in Blackpool saw Littler become only the fourth player in tournament history to win back-to-back titles, and the first in a decade to achieve the feat. It also keeps alive his bid to complete a clean sweep of the major titles across the year.

He already has the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League, Masters, and now the Matchplay. He is also defending the Grand Slam, Grand Prix and the Players Championship Finals later this year and hunting a European Championship win to hold every single premier title.

For Webster, Littler's run at the Matchplay marks the greatest major display in the history of the sport and is another sign that the world No 1 is increasingly likely to eventually hold every major trophy the sport has to offer simultaneously.

"This is what I keep saying - what do the other players cling on to now? Where is the weakness? What do you do," Webster said.

"He is playing fantastic at the minute and he is making his opponents miss. It is a recipe for dominance.

"The tournament average has been in the back of his mind. He is setting himself a challenge inside a challenge.

"Winning a major is a huge thing to do but he is setting little challenges within that.

"It is going to get to the point where he is going to be leaving 170s and things like that because he is dominating contests.

"He is just in a completely dominant mood. He trusts everything he does. You just have to admire it. We probably think he can't get better but he is going to try.

"He is going to keep craving tournament averages - he just has that will to win.

"This has to be the greatest campaign at a major, doesn't it? This has to be it. If you look at the stats alone, he has a tournament average of 111.

"It is an incredible achievement and it is one that in 12 months time he will try to eclipse.

"I half expect it [for him to win every major in 2026].

"I don't see where you are going to get him. European champs maybe? Players championship? I am just throwing things out there.

"It is going to be tough for the rest of them."

Time to 'take stock' as Littler sends a message to the pack

For those chasing Littler down, the question is what do you do next?

Records have fallen, he has dominated in Blackpool, and has already set his sights on what he needs to do next in order to continue this remarkable run.

And it truly is remarkable - his last defeat in a major tournament that went beyond 20 legs came against Luke Humphries in the World Darts championship back in 2024.

Can they stop what seems inevitable? Webster thinks it will take "new standards" to even get close to him.

"It just sends out a message now to the rest of the pack of the standard you have to reach to get anywhere near him.

"Every player from this event will take stock of what happened.

"Someone like Luke Humphries, it won't wash for him being knocked out in the first round so he will need to refocus.

"Michael van Gerwen has got a huge end to the year. I think he is down at world No 7 now which feels strange to say.

"There is some work for him to do there now - he was a finalist at the World Darts Championship two years ago so there is some more money coming off.

"After every tournament you have to take stock, look at what you need to improve on, and get ready for what is the business end of the year now."

articles.title: World Matchplay Darts: Luke Littler draws fresh Phil Taylor comparisons after historic record-breaking Blackpool victory
articles.summary: Luke Littler posted the highest tournament average in World Matchplay Darts history to successfully defend his title in Blackpool; Littler thrashed Gerwyn Price to continue his run of winning every PDC major title in 2026 and receive fresh praise
articles.body:
Luke Littler has reiterated his dream to become the ‘greatest darts player ever’ after his dominant Betfred World Matchplay title defence, with the world No 1’s latest win drawing further comparisons to Phil Taylor’s past record-breaking success.

Littler capped off a historic week at Blackpool's Winter Gardens becoming the first player since Michael van Gerwen to successfully defend his title, continuing his record of winning every PDC major title in 2026 so far.

The book of darting superlatives is rapidly running out of pages to describe Littler's brilliance, with the teenager continuing to climb to generational heights in the sport and overtake many records held by childhood idol Taylor.

  • How Luke Littler stormed to another Blackpool win
  • Littler: Win 'one of the best weeks of my life'
  • Got Sky? Watch on the Sky Sports app 📱
  • Not got Sky? Get instant access with NOW 📺

Littler had already defended titles at the World Championship and the UK Open, plus won the Winmau World Masters, Premier League and the World Cup of Darts, with the 19-year-old now chasing more success in the months and years ahead.

"I don't think anyone has ever won every major in the calendar year and that is what we are pushing for," Littler told Sky Sports. "The family, they are always backing me a million per cent and that is what drives me on.

"I would absolutely love to be the greatest dart player there ever has been. As I have always said, I have got to win 16 of these, 16 worlds, and then have a look at whatever else Phil Taylor did win.

"I have got plenty more years. When am I going to retire? Who knows. I have still got plenty more years left in the tank."

Littler smashed the highest tournament average, posting 111.04 across his five matches to beat Taylor's 2010 previous best of 106.31, plus broke his own record of most 180s at a World Matchplay.

"I am very happy with myself and the performances, not only in the final but the past eight days, every round," Littler added. "It is crazy to say that the 109 average was my worst average throughout the tournament!"

Why time is required in Taylor comparisons

Littler may have his hands back on the trophy named after Taylor, but he would need to win every World Matchplay until 2040 just to equal the all-time title tally of 'The Power'.

In 2007, six months after Luke Littler was born, Phil Taylor made a quarter-final exit at the World Matchplay - just the second time this century that 'The Power' had been beaten on the Winter Gardens stage.

Seven years later, the week after Littler left year two of primary school, Taylor had still not lost another match at the event and was closing out a seventh consecutive World Matchplay title.

Taylor won a record 38 consecutive matches during that title streak and lost just eight times in his 24-year career at the World Matchplay, with no player since coming remotely close to beating those extraordinary achievements.

The trophy comparisons may be a mismatch but the scoring differences between the two are certainly not, with Littler posting the second-highest tournament winning average in the sport's history and just 0.5 points behind Taylor's 2009 European Championship win - despite playing over double the legs Taylor did that week

"I can still get better," Littler insisted in his press conference. "I can obviously get a lot better. Through the matches I was up to a 120 average at one point. I didn't stick at it, but maybe in a few years' time I will stick at it and go up to that when the match is finished.

"At the minute, I'm playing some of the best stuff and I've just got to keep it there."

Littler was described by Price as "one in a million" and has taken plenty of plaudits from his peers for his run to another TV title, with his success more impressive given the growing depth at the top of sport.

"Luke's dominance over the last 12 months has been very Taylor-esque and that's why he's reached that figure (£3m in prize money), which is a huge figure and one that we've never had before," PDC chief executive Matt Porter told Sky Sports.

"I don't think the mentality of the opponents is the same (as Taylor's era). 20-odd years ago, players would see getting to the final as their championship.

"You wouldn't get that answer off Gerwyn Price, you wouldn't get it off Luke Humphries, Michael Van Gerwen, Steven Bunting, Nathan Aspinall, Jonny Clayton - those guys are not here to make up the numbers.

"Luke at the moment is almost unstoppable. Nobody's ever unstoppable, but with the way he's playing, someone's really going to have to up their game if they're going to beat him."

What's next for Littler?

Further title defences at the Boyle Sports World Grand Prix (September 28-October 4) and Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts (November 14-22) are to come for Littler, who already holds a record-breaking advantage at the top of PDC rankings.

Littler will look to claim his elusive TV ranked title at the European Championship (October 22-25), while winning all three would leave him just requiring the Players Championship Finals (November 27-29) to complete a sweep of every major and big TV event in a calendar year.

Phil Taylor's impressive 2009 season didn't contain the Premier League title or the World Cup of Darts, which didn't launch until the following year, while Van Gerwen's 2016 dominance was also missing World Cup glory. Littler has the chance to surpass both with his campaign.

Littler has been skipping ProTour events during the season to leave qualification for the Players Championship Finals in doubt, although his latest win - and thoughts of claiming all the majors in the same - has changed his schedule plans over the coming months.

"Coming into the tournament I'd won every major so far so this is what I wanted to do," Littler explained. "I have been checking the Pro Tour rankings - whoever is in 64th (final qualification spot) just keeps going up and up!

"I know there is four (Players Championship events) in Leicester I have got to go to now. If I don't qualify I will get grilled and if I qualify I will get grilled anyway, so who knows what is going to happen."

Littler has already cemented himself as one of the darting greats in just over two and a half years as a professional. The thought of him getting even better in pursuit of more records is a terrifying - but exciting - prospect.

articles.title: Luke Littler: What does rest of 2026 look like for world No 1 as he targets the clean sweep of majors after World Matchplay triumph
articles.summary: Luke Littler is targeting a clean sweep of majors in 2026 but what exactly does he need to still win? He has already won the World Darts Championship, UK Open, Premier League, Masters and the Matchplay in 2026
articles.body:
When Luke Littler arrived in Blackpool for the World Matchplay he made one thing clear: the outcome of this tournament would determine how the rest of his 2026 unfolded.

"The next nine days will decide if I go to the Players Championship Finals," Littler told Sky Sports on opening night.

"If I don't win this then I'm not going back to Minehead for the Players Championship Finals. If I do win this then I will have to go to some Pro Tours and try and get in there."
